465	######## captions/on-device-transcription
466	---
467	title: "Transcribe on this Mac"
468	description: Turn the speech in your clips into captions with your Mac's own speech recogniser, with no key, no upload and no length limit, and install the languages you need.
469	---
470	
471	
472	**On this Mac** is the free engine for [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/). It recognises speech with the recogniser built into your Mac, so it costs nothing, needs no key, and your audio never leaves the machine.
473	
474	<AtAGlance
475	  menu="File ▸ Generate Captions…"
476	  where="Generate Captions sheet ▸ Engine: ▸ On this Mac"
477	  tools={['transcribe', 'get_transcript']}
478	  needs="The language's speech model, installed on this Mac. No key, and nothing is uploaded."
479	/>
480	
481	## Transcribe on this Mac
482	
483	<Steps>
484	
485	1. Choose **File ▸ Generate Captions…**.
486	
487	2. Set **Engine:** to **On this Mac**. The sheet remembers the engine you chose last.
488	
489	3. Check **Language:**. If it reads "— not installed", [download the language](#download-a-speech-language) first.
490	
491	4. Choose **Generate**.
492	
493	</Steps>
494	
495	<Shot
496	  name="15-generate-captions-sheet.sheet"
497	  alt="The Generate Captions sheet with Language set to English (United States), Engine set to On this Mac, From set to Whole timeline and Style set to Subtitles. The paragraph at the top says the words are recognised on this Mac and nothing is uploaded, and the summary reads 2 clips, 00:00:10.200 of audio."
498	/>
499	
500	The sheet says what it's about to do: "The words are recognised ON THIS MAC and land as ordinary text clips on a track of their own, so they show in the preview and burn into an export with no further step. Nothing is uploaded."
501	
502	Frame Job extracts the part of the media each clip plays, and recognises that. There's no length limit, and macOS shows no permission prompt. The recogniser reads an extracted audio file and never touches the microphone.
503	
504	[Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) covers the rest of the sheet: which clips to caption, the style and the progress card. The other engine is [AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/), which runs in the cloud on your own key.
505	
506	## Choose a language
507	
508	**Language:** lists every language this Mac's recogniser supports, by name, so the list differs from Mac to Mac. It opens on your Mac's own language, or the nearest one on the list.
509	
510	A language whose speech model isn't on this Mac reads "— not installed". **Generate** stays greyed until the chosen language is installed.
511	
512	If the recogniser names no language at all, the pop-up reads **No on-device language** and the note under the summary says "This Mac's speech engine named no language with an on-device speech model. Reopen this sheet to ask it again." Setting **Engine:** to **AssemblyAI** still works in that state.
513	
514	## Download a speech language
515	
516	Speech models are installed per Mac, not per project, and this sheet is the only place Frame Job installs one.
517	
518	<Steps>
519	
520	1. Choose a language marked "— not installed". A **Download** button appears under **Language:**.
521	
522	2. Choose **Download**.
523	
524	3. Wait for the row to finish. It shows a bar and "Downloading *language*…".
525	
526	</Steps>
527	
528	When the download finishes, the language is installed and selected, and **Generate** comes on.
529	
530	The bar moves without a figure until the download reports its size. Only then does the row add a percentage, such as "Downloading French… 40%". It never shows a size.
531	
532	While the download runs:
533	
534	- **Language:** and **Engine:** are locked, and **Generate** stays greyed.
535	- **Download** becomes **Cancel**, which is greyed until the download has started reporting. Choosing it stops the download with no message.
536	- The **Cancel** at the bottom of the sheet closes the sheet and leaves the download running. You lose the bar and the way to stop it.
537	
538	If the download fails, the note reads "The download did not finish:" and gives the reason. The **Download** button is back, so you can try again.
539	
540	## Every run recognises the audio again
541	
542	Nothing is kept between runs for captions made on this Mac. Each run, [restyling](/captions/restyle-captions/) included, recognises the audio from the start. That's free, but it takes the time again.
543	
544	The sheet's preview never shows on-device words either. It shows the first words of a kept [AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/#reuse-a-transcript) transcript if the clip has one, and "This is how it looks" if not.
545	
546	The [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-words/) does keep the words it recognises on this Mac, but those are separate, and captions never use them.
547	
548	## The pause note
549	
550	With **On this Mac** chosen and a [word style](/captions/word-caption-styles/) picked, a note under the look boxes reads "On-device words rarely carry a pause; this shows mostly with AssemblyAI." It shows whether or not **Dim in pauses** is ticked.
551	
552	The recogniser starts each word early, so the word after a pause starts inside the silence, and few gaps are left for [Dim in pauses](/captions/word-caption-looks/) to act on. The look still works, but you'll see it rarely.
553	
554	## With an agent
555	
556	`transcribe` uses this engine by default, whatever the sheet last chose.
557	
558	An agent can't install a language, and `transcribe` never downloads one. A language tag that speech recognition doesn't know stops the call with "check the tag's spelling" and the tags it does know. A tag it knows with no model on this Mac stops the call with "A person has to install it", the steps in this sheet, and the languages that are ready. Nothing changes in either case. `get_transcript` works to the same rules. See [`transcribe`](/mcp/tools-captions/#transcribe).

569	######## captions/assemblyai-transcription
570	---
571	title: "Transcribe with AssemblyAI"
572	description: Send the audio of your files to AssemblyAI on your own key for captions with speakers, a vocabulary and language detection, see the price first, and reuse each transcript for free.
573	---
574	
575	
576	**AssemblyAI** is the cloud engine for captions. It adds speaker labels, a vocabulary of names and jargon, and language detection, and its word timing shows real pauses. You pay AssemblyAI directly on your own key, and each file's transcript is kept so you only pay for it once.
577	
578	<AtAGlance
579	  menu="File ▸ Generate Captions…"
580	  where="Generate Captions sheet ▸ Engine: ▸ AssemblyAI"
581	  tools="transcribe"
582	  needs="Your own AssemblyAI key, unless every file is already transcribed, and a network connection for anything new."
583	/>
584	
585	## Transcribe with AssemblyAI
586	
587	<Steps>
588	
589	1. [Save your AssemblyAI key](/captions/assemblyai-key/) in Settings, if you haven't.
590	
591	2. Choose **File ▸ Generate Captions…**.
592	
593	3. Set **Engine:** to **AssemblyAI**. The **Speakers:**, **Vocabulary:** and **Transcribe again:** rows appear.
594	
595	4. Set [**Language:**](#choose-a-language), and turn on [**Speakers:**](#split-the-words-by-speaker) or fill in [**Vocabulary:**](#add-names-and-jargon) if you want them.
596	
597	5. Read the [price](#the-price-before-you-press-generate) in the summary line.
598	
599	6. Choose **Generate**. Nothing is uploaded until you do.
600	
601	</Steps>
602	
603	The paragraph at the top of the sheet reads "The audio of these files is uploaded to AssemblyAI (United States), transcribed with Universal-3.5 Pro, and deleted from AssemblyAI once the words have been read back. Nothing is uploaded until Generate is pressed." It names your [region](/captions/assemblyai-key/#choose-a-region), which is United States or European Union.
604	
605	Each media file goes up once, and every clip on it takes its words from that one transcript. Frame Job asks for Universal-3.5 Pro and allows Universal-2 as a fallback. This engine doesn't use your Mac's speech models, so it works on a Mac that has none.
606	
607	[What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/) says exactly what leaves your Mac and how it's deleted. [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) covers the rest of the sheet.
608	
609	## Split the words by speaker
610	
611	Tick **Speakers:** ("split by speaker, coloured in Subtitles") to have AssemblyAI label who says what. It's off by default and adds $0.02 an hour to the price.
612	
613	A change of speaker then always starts a new caption: a new cue in [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/), or a new page in a [word style](/captions/word-caption-styles/). In the Subtitles style, each speaker's cues also take their own colour.
614	
615	Speakers are counted separately for each media file. A speaker is a label within one file, so the same person in two files can come back as two different speakers.
616	
617	## Add names and jargon
618	
619	Type the words you expect into **Vocabulary:**, separated by commas: product names, people, identifiers. They go to AssemblyAI with the request. The field starts empty, and its placeholder reads "names and jargon, separated by commas".
620	
621	Blank entries and exact repeats are dropped. The list stops at 1,000 terms, which is AssemblyAI's limit, and it's cut from the end, so put the terms that matter most first. When the limit cuts your list, the note reads "Vocabulary was capped at 1000 terms (AssemblyAI's limit); N were given."
622	
623	## Choose a language
624	
625	**Language:** opens on **Detect automatically**, which leaves the language to AssemblyAI. The [result](#what-the-result-says) then tells you what it found.
626	
627	You can also name one: English, English (Australia), English (United Kingdom), English (United States), Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Arabic, Danish, Dutch, Finnish, Hebrew, Hindi, Japanese, Chinese, Norwegian, Swedish, Turkish or Vietnamese. That list is what AssemblyAI published on 2026-09-17, so it can fall behind.
628	
629	## The price before you press Generate
630	
631	The summary line prices the run at AssemblyAI's published rate, and updates as you change a control:
632	
633	`2 files to upload · 01:12:30.000 of audio · about $0.25 at AssemblyAI's published rate · 1 file already transcribed`
634	
635	The rate is $0.21 an hour of audio, plus $0.02 an hour with **Speakers:** on. Those are the figures AssemblyAI published on 2026-09-17. They're built into Frame Job and aren't fetched, so AssemblyAI's own bill is the real figure. Each file is priced at its whole length, because AssemblyAI [bills for the whole file](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/#what-is-uploaded-and-billed).
636	
637	A very short run reads "under $0.01". When every file is already transcribed the line starts "Nothing to upload", as in `Nothing to upload · 2 files already transcribed`.
638	
639	Two more counts can appear, and neither is in the price:
640	
641	| The line says | What it means |
642	| --- | --- |
643	| "1 file waiting on an earlier delete" | The file [isn't uploaded](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/#a-pending-delete-holds-a-file-back) until AssemblyAI confirms an earlier delete. |
644	| "1 file could not be read" | Frame Job couldn't read the media file, so it can't be transcribed. With nothing else to do, **Generate** is greyed. |
645	
646	## Why each file uploads
647	
648	Rest the pointer on the summary line. You get one line for each file that isn't already transcribed, saying why, and then the rate as a dated sentence.
649	
650	| The line says | What changed |
651	| --- | --- |
652	| "has not been transcribed yet" | This file has no transcript in the project. |
653	| "has changed since it was transcribed" | The file on disk isn't the one that was transcribed. |
654	| "was transcribed with a different language" | The named setting differs from the transcript's. It can also name **model**, **speakers** or **vocabulary**, or several of them. |
655	| "was transcribed for a different request" | Something else about the request differs. |
656	| "is already transcribed, and Transcribe again was asked for" | You ticked [Transcribe again](#transcribe-again). |
657	| "could not be read, so it cannot be transcribed" | The media file couldn't be read. |
658	
659	## Reuse a transcript
660	
661	Each media file's transcript is kept in the project package, every word as AssemblyAI sent it. A later run that wants the same transcript uses it, with no upload, no request and no cost.
662	
663	A transcript is reused when all of these match:
664	
665	- **The file:** its size, modified time and duration, and whether it has audio. Change the file, or relink to a different one, and it's transcribed again.
666	- **The model** Frame Job asks for.
667	- **The language:** **Detect automatically** and a named language count as different, as do two named languages.
668	- **Speakers:** on or off.
669	- **Vocabulary:** the same terms in the same order.
670	
671	The caption style and the looks don't count, so [restyling](/captions/restyle-captions/) never uploads. Your region doesn't count either, so changing it uploads nothing again.
672	
673	A transcript made for [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/) serves captions too, as long as those settings match.
674	
675	The transcript belongs to the media entry, not the file on disk. Two media entries over the same file are uploaded and billed separately.
676	
677	## Transcribe again
678	
679	Tick **Transcribe again:** ("ignore any cached transcript") to ignore what's kept and ask AssemblyAI again. It's off by default. Each file goes up in full and is billed again, and the summary line shows that price.
680	
681	Frame Job won't do this for a file with a [pending delete](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/#a-pending-delete-holds-a-file-back) until the delete goes through.
682	
683	## Generate with no key
684	
685	With no key set, the note reads "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription.", **Generate** is greyed, and resting the pointer on it shows the same sentence. Saving a key in Settings turns **Generate** on with the sheet still open.
686	
687	The exception is work you've already paid for. When every file in the run has a current transcript, **Generate** works with no key, and the paragraph at the top changes to "Current cached transcripts will be used without an API key or network request." Ticking **Transcribe again:** ends that, because it needs a new upload.
688	
689	With a key set the paragraph stays as it is, and the summary line says there's nothing to upload.
690	
691	## Transcribe an untitled project
692	
693	You don't have to save first. An untitled project's transcripts stay in a temporary folder and move into the project package on its first save. Close the project without saving and they're gone, so the same files would be paid for again in a new project. The record of any [delete still pending](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/#what-the-result-warns-about) goes with them.
694	
695	In the rare case that a project has no folder to keep transcripts in at all, the note reads "This project has nowhere to keep its transcript cache, so it cannot be transcribed with AssemblyAI. Save it first." Save the project and carry on.
696	
697	## What the result says
698	
699	While a run goes, the detail line on the sheet's progress card shows the stage for each file: "Extracting", "Uploading" with the megabytes sent, "Submitting", "Waiting for AssemblyAI" with the seconds so far, and "Saving".
700	
701	A run with nothing to report closes the sheet by itself. If there is something, the card stays open with **Close**, and these lines can join the usual count of captions added:
702	
703	| The card says | What it means |
704	| --- | --- |
705	| "“interview.mov”: detected Spanish (97% confidence)." | With **Detect automatically**, the language AssemblyAI found in each file it just transcribed, and how sure it was. The figure is left out if AssemblyAI gave none. |
706	| "“interview.mov” was transcribed with universal-2, not universal-3-5-pro." | AssemblyAI used the fallback model. |
707	| "The transcript of “interview.mov” could not be kept in the project for reuse." | The captions are fine, but a later run may upload and bill this file again. |
708	| "AssemblyAI has not confirmed deleting the transcript of…" | See [What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/#what-the-result-warns-about). |
709	
710	## When a file fails
711	
712	One file's failure doesn't end a run. Its clips are listed with the reason, and captions from the other files are still placed. If every file fails, nothing is placed and the card shows why.
713	
714	Two things end a run early, and neither places anything: choosing **Cancel**, and a key AssemblyAI turns down, because every later upload would fail the same way. Files that had already finished stay in the project, so a later run doesn't pay for them again.
715	
716	| The reason reads | What happened |
717	| --- | --- |
718	| "No network connection" | Frame Job couldn't reach AssemblyAI. |
719	| "AssemblyAI refused the API key — check it in Frame Job ▸ Settings" | AssemblyAI turned the key down, and the run stops there. Try **Verify** in [Settings](/captions/assemblyai-key/#check-the-key). |
720	| "AssemblyAI answered 500" | AssemblyAI had a problem of its own. The number varies. |
721	| "AssemblyAI did not finish the transcript in the time allowed." | Frame Job waits at least 5 minutes for a transcript, and longer for audio over about 4 hours. |
722	| "“name” is longer than AssemblyAI's 10-hour limit for one file." | Nothing was sent for this file. |
723	| "AssemblyAI may have created a transcript, but Frame Job could not recover its ID…" | AssemblyAI's reply never reached Frame Job. Check your AssemblyAI dashboard before you try again, because the transcript may still be there. |
724	| AssemblyAI's own sentence | AssemblyAI turned the request down or couldn't transcribe the file, perhaps over a problem with your account, and Frame Job passes on its words. |
725	
726	A failed upload is tried once more, unless AssemblyAI turned it down outright. While waiting, Frame Job checks on the transcript every 3 seconds and rides out up to 3 failed checks in a row. It never follows a redirect, so your key can't reach another host, and the run reports that instead.
727	
728	## Filler words stay out of captions
729	
730	AssemblyAI's words include fillers, and captions leave them out, so a caption reads the same whether or not its transcript has them. The sheet's preview leaves them out too.
731	
732	The words left out are um, uh, hmm, mhm, uh-huh, ah, huh, hm, m, er and erm, in any case and with any punctuation at their edges. The kept transcript still has them, which is what lets [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/) find them later.
733	
734	## With an agent
735	
736	`transcribe` never picks this engine by itself: an agent has to pass `engine: "assemblyai"` on each call, whatever the sheet last chose. It can pass any language code, and one AssemblyAI doesn't support comes back as AssemblyAI's own sentence after the upload.
737	
738	`speakers`, `vocabulary` and `refresh` are the sheet's **Speakers:**, **Vocabulary:** and **Transcribe again:**. They work only with this engine, and the call stops if an agent passes one with `engine: "apple"`.
739	
740	Beside the usual result, a run reports `uploaded`, `cached`, `audio_seconds`, `speech_model_used`, `language_detected`, `endpoint` and, when there's something to say, `note`. A second run over the same files lists them under `cached`.
741	
742	The built-in [Assistant](/assistant/privacy/) can't use this engine at all. Use **File ▸ Generate Captions…**, which shows what's uploaded and what it costs.
743	
744	See [`transcribe`](/mcp/tools-captions/#transcribe).

756	######## captions/assemblyai-privacy
757	---
758	title: "What goes to AssemblyAI"
759	description: What leaves your Mac when you transcribe with AssemblyAI, what you're billed for, how the transcript is deleted afterwards, and what happens when a delete doesn't land.
760	---
761	
762	
763	When you transcribe with AssemblyAI, the sound of your files leaves your Mac, and only after you press **Generate**. Frame Job then asks AssemblyAI to delete its transcript as soon as it has the words. Captions made [on this Mac](/captions/on-device-transcription/) never leave it.
764	
765	<AtAGlance
766	  menu={['File ▸ Generate Captions…', 'Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…']}
767	  where="Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription ▸ ⓘ"
768	  tools={['transcribe', 'transcribe_for_fillers']}
769	  needs="Your own AssemblyAI key."
770	/>
771	
772	## What is uploaded and billed
773	
774	| Goes to AssemblyAI | Stays on your Mac |
775	| --- | --- |
776	| The whole audio of each media file behind the chosen clips | The video |
777	| Your **Vocabulary:** terms, and the language and **Speakers:** settings | The project and the rest of its media |
778	
779	The audio goes up as 16 kHz mono FLAC, about half the size of a WAV with the same samples. If the FLAC can't be written, a WAV goes up instead. Frame Job removes its temporary copy from your Mac when the upload ends, whether or not it worked.
780	
781	It's the whole file, not only the parts your clips use, and AssemblyAI bills for the whole file. A two-hour recording you use 30 seconds of costs two hours, about $0.42 at the rate [Frame Job shows](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/#the-price-before-you-press-generate). A file over 10 hours is turned down before anything is sent.
782	
783	The audio goes to the [region](/captions/assemblyai-key/#choose-a-region) set in Settings, and the sheet names that region before you press **Generate**. **Transcribe** in [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/) sends audio in the same way.
784	
785	:::caution
786	A recording of someone else goes to a third party here. Get their say-so first, or use **On this Mac**. The `transcribe` tool gives an agent the same warning.
787	:::
788	
789	## The transcript is deleted after reading
790	
791	Each file's round trip runs in this order: upload, transcribe, read the words back, save them in the project package, then ask AssemblyAI to delete its transcript. You don't have to do anything. Each delete request has 5 seconds to answer.
792	
793	Frame Job also asks for the delete when a transcript fails, runs out of time or can't be used, and when you choose **Cancel** while AssemblyAI is working.
794	
795	A copy of the words stays in your [project package](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/#reuse-a-transcript). That copy is what makes later runs free.
796	
797	If AssemblyAI doesn't confirm the delete, [the result says so](#what-the-result-warns-about).
798	
799	## Unconfirmed deletes are retried
800	
801	An unconfirmed delete is retried at the start of the next AssemblyAI run in the same project that has a key. Every delete still waiting in the project is retried then, whichever files the run is about.
802	
803	The retry uses the key and region set at that later run, so it can only work with a key for the account and region that made the upload. The two regions don't share transcripts. If you've changed either since, set it back for a run.
804	
805	With no key set when that next run starts, nothing is sent, and the delete waits for a run that has one.
806	
807	## A pending delete holds a file back
808	
809	While a delete is pending, Frame Job won't upload that file again, because the kept transcript is its only record of the delete still to be made. If that file's kept transcript still matches the run, it's used as normal. If the file needs a new upload, or you ticked [Transcribe again](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/#transcribe-again), it waits:
810	
811	- The summary line counts it apart, as "1 file waiting on an earlier delete", and leaves it out of the price.
812	- Resting the pointer on the summary gives its price: "It is waiting on an earlier delete and will not be uploaded in this run — about $0.42 more if it does."
813	
814	The hover line says "if it does" because the retry happens first. If the delete goes through at the start of the run, the file uploads in that same run. If it doesn't, the file isn't uploaded, and its clips are listed with the reason "AssemblyAI has not confirmed deleting its earlier transcript, so it was not uploaded again; the next run with an API key retries the delete".
815	
816	## What the result warns about
817	
818	These lines appear on the sheet's result card, with the file's name in place of "name".
819	
820	| The card says | What to do |
821	| --- | --- |
822	| "AssemblyAI has not confirmed deleting the transcript of “name”; it will be retried at the next run with an API key." | Nothing. Run AssemblyAI again in this project when you next need it, with the same account and region. |
823	| "…It was not uploaded again in this run." | Added to the line above when the delete held the file back. |
824	| "AssemblyAI has not confirmed deleting the transcript of “name”; cleanup was deferred because no API key is set. Its deletion ID is retained in the project; a later run with a key for the originating account and region will retry deletion only if that ID is safe to send." | Set the key for that account and region, then run again in this project. |
825	| "AssemblyAI has not confirmed deleting the transcript of “name”. Its transcript could not be saved in the project, so Frame Job cannot retry deleting it automatically. Delete it in your AssemblyAI dashboard." | Frame Job has no record to retry from. Choose [Account Page](/captions/assemblyai-key/#open-your-assemblyai-account) in Settings and delete it there. |
826	
827	:::caution
828	In an [untitled project](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/#transcribe-an-untitled-project), the record of a pending delete lives in a temporary folder. If you never save the project, that record is lost and Frame Job can't retry. Save the project, or delete the transcript in your AssemblyAI dashboard.
829	:::

840	######## captions/assemblyai-key
841	---
842	title: "Your AssemblyAI key"
843	description: Save, check and remove the AssemblyAI key that turns on cloud captions and Remove Filler Words, choose your region, and see where the key is kept.
844	---
845	
846	
847	Your AssemblyAI key turns on cloud transcription, and AssemblyAI bills your account directly. It lives in Settings, so it's the same for every project, and you can set it with no project open. For how keys work across Frame Job, see [AI features and your own keys](/getting-started/ai-and-your-keys/).
848	
849	<AtAGlance
850	  menu="Frame Job ▸ Settings…"
851	  keys="⌘,"
852	  where="Settings ▸ Transcription"
853	  needs="An AssemblyAI account."
854	/>
855	
856	<Shot
857	  name="02-settings.window"
858	  alt="The Settings window. Under the Transcription heading, with its info button, are an AssemblyAI API key field reading Paste your key, a Region pop-up set to United States, the line No API key is set, and the buttons Save, Remove, Verify and Account Page. Remove and Verify are greyed."
859	/>
860	
861	## Save your AssemblyAI key
862	
863	<Steps>
864	
865	1. Choose **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** (<kbd>⌘,</kbd>) and find **Transcription**.
866	
867	2. Choose **Account Page** to get a key from your AssemblyAI dashboard.
868	
869	3. Paste the key into **AssemblyAI API key:**.
870	
871	4. Choose **Save**, or press <kbd>↩</kbd>.
872	
873	5. Choose [**Verify**](#check-the-key) to check that it works.
874	
875	</Steps>
876	
877	The line under **Region:** says "Key saved.", and the field empties. From then on the field shows a fixed row of dots, the same length whatever your key is. The key itself never goes back in the field, so it can't be read or copied out of the window.
878	
879	With no key anywhere, the line reads "No API key is set." in ordinary grey. That isn't an error. **Save** with an empty field beeps and does nothing.
880	
881	If the key file can't be written, the line reads "The API key could not be saved:" and gives the reason. The field is emptied anyway, so paste the key again once it's fixed.
882	
883	## Check the key
884	
885	**Verify** makes AssemblyAI's cheapest signed-in request, with your key and region, to see if the key works. It doesn't transcribe or bill anything.
886	
887	It checks the key typed in the field, even if you haven't saved it, then the saved key, then [the environment's](#use-a-key-from-the-environment). A typed key is only checked, so choose **Save** as well to keep it. A run never uses a key that's only typed.
888	
889	| The line says | What it means |
890	| --- | --- |
891	| "Checking…" | The request is on its way. |
892	| "Key accepted" | AssemblyAI accepted the key in this region. |
893	| "No API key is set." | There was no key to check. |
894	| "Settings changed since this check began. Verify again." | You changed the key or the region during the check, so its answer no longer applies. |
895	| AssemblyAI's message, such as "AssemblyAI refused the API key — check it in Frame Job ▸ Settings" | The check failed, and the message says why. "No network connection" is another. |
896	
897	**Verify** is greyed when there's no key at all, and while a check of the same key and region is running.
898	
899	## Choose a region
900	
901	**Region:** chooses the AssemblyAI data centre your audio goes to: **United States**, the default, or **European Union**. It's saved as soon as you pick it, and an open sheet updates straight away. The Generate Captions and Remove Filler Words sheets name the region before you upload.
902	
903	A transcript made in one region can't be seen from the other, so pick the region your account uses. [A pending delete](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/#unconfirmed-deletes-are-retried) only succeeds in the region it was made in.
904	
905	Changing the region doesn't upload anything again. Transcripts already kept in a project stay usable.
906	
907	## Open your AssemblyAI account
908	
909	**Account Page** opens your AssemblyAI dashboard in your browser, at `https://www.assemblyai.com/dashboard`. That's where you get a key and see what you've spent.
910	
911	## Remove the key
912	
913	**Remove** deletes the saved key and says "Key removed." It's greyed unless a key is saved.
914	
915	If the removal fails, the key stays saved and the line says why.
916	
917	## Where the key is kept
918	
919	The key is saved in a file only your account can read, not in the Keychain:
920	
921	`~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/assemblyai-key`
922	
923	The file's mode is `0600`, and it sits beside `anthropic-key`, the [Assistant](/assistant/set-up/)'s key. Any program running as you can read it, so treat that file like a password. The key is never passed on the command line.
924	
925	## Use a key from the environment
926	
927	If no key is saved, Frame Job also accepts one from the `RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY` environment variable, which is useful when you launch it from a terminal.
928	
929	- A saved key always wins over the variable.
930	- An empty variable counts as no key.
931	- **Verify** checks the variable's key when nothing is typed or saved.
932	- **Remove** stays greyed, because nothing is saved.
933	
934	See [Where Frame Job keeps its files](/reference/file-locations/).
935	
936	## What the key turns on
937	
938	| Feature | Without a key |
939	| --- | --- |
940	| The **AssemblyAI** engine of [Generate Captions](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/) | **Generate** is greyed, [unless every file is already transcribed](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/#generate-with-no-key). |
941	| [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/), which finds fillers only through AssemblyAI | The menu item is greyed and reads **Remove Filler Words… (needs your AssemblyAI key)**, unless a file the command would read already has a transcript made with filler words. See [Transcripts for filler words](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/) for what works without one. |
942	
943	Captions made [on this Mac](/captions/on-device-transcription/) need no key.
944	
945	Saving or removing a key, or changing the region, reaches an open Generate Captions sheet straight away, so **Generate** can come on without reopening it.
946	
947	## What the info button says
948	
949	The ⓘ beside the **Transcription** heading explains three things:
950	
951	- **What leaves your Mac.** The audio of the files you're captioning is uploaded, transcribed, read back and then deleted from AssemblyAI. A delete that didn't land is retried at the start of the next run. Nothing is uploaded until you press **Generate**, and captions made on this Mac never leave it.
952	- **The rate.** AssemblyAI's published rate as Frame Job last read it: $0.21 an hour of audio, and $0.02 more with **Speakers:** on, read on 2026-09-17.
953	- **The key.** It's kept in a file only you can read and is never shown again once it's saved.
954	
955	[What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/) has the full story.
956	
957	## Only a person sets the key
958	
959	No agent tool can read or change the key or the region, and an agent can't pass a key of its own. Only you set them, here. An agent's [`transcribe`](/mcp/tools-captions/#transcribe) call uses your saved key, or the environment's. With neither, it stops with the same "No AssemblyAI API key is set." sentence, unless every file is already transcribed.
960

976	The Subtitles style turns speech into classic two-line cues, the kind you'd see on a film or a broadcast. Each cue is a text clip in the **Caption** preset.
977

990	## Make subtitles
991	
992	<Steps>
993	
994	1. Choose **File ▸ Generate Captions…**.
995	
996	2. Set **Language:**, **Engine:** and **From:**. [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) explains each one.
997	
998	3. Set **Style:** to **Subtitles**. The sheet opens on the last style you chose, and on Subtitles the first time.
999	
1000	4. Choose **Generate**.
1001	
1002	</Steps>
1003	
1004	The cues land on a new track at the front of the stack, called **Captions**, or **Captions 2** and so on if that name is taken. The whole run is one undo step, **Generate Captions**.
1005	
1006	## The Subtitles style
1007	
1008	Frame Job builds each cue from the recognised words by these rules:
1009	
1010	| Rule | Limit |
1011	| --- | --- |
1012	| Lines in a cue | At most 2 |
1013	| Characters on a line | At most 42 |
1014	| Time on screen | At most 6 seconds, up to the end of the cue's last word |
1015	| Gap between cues | At least one frame |
1016	| Speakers in a cue | One. A change of speaker always starts a new cue. |
1017	
1018	A cue starts on its first word and ends with its last, so it doesn't stay up through a long silence. A word too long for a line is left whole, never hyphenated, and wraps inside the caption box.
1019	
1020	## Speaker colours
1021	
1022	Each speaker's cues can take their own colour, so a viewer can tell who's talking.
1023	
1024	<Steps>
1025	
1026	1. Set **Engine:** to **AssemblyAI**. The **Speakers:** row is hidden with **On this Mac**, and a new AssemblyAI transcription needs [your key](/captions/assemblyai-key/).
1027	
1028	2. Tick **Speakers:**, which reads "split by speaker, coloured in Subtitles".
1029	
1030	3. Set **Style:** to **Subtitles** and choose **Generate**.
1031	
1032	</Steps>
1033	
1034	Speakers take their colours in the order they first appear in the run: white, yellow, cyan, green, then round again. The fifth speaker is white like the first. The colours are a fixed table with no setting. To change one afterwards, select those cues and set the colour under **Text** in the [Clip tab](/text-and-shapes/text-style/).
1035	
1036	Speakers are told apart within each media file, so the first speaker in one file and the first speaker in another count as two people and take two colours.
1037	
1038	Speaker colours only apply to the Subtitles style. In a [word caption style](/captions/word-caption-styles/), a change of speaker starts a new page and the colours stay as the style draws them.
1039	
1040	## The Caption preset
1041	
1042	Every cue is drawn in the **Caption** [text preset](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/), whether it was generated or [imported from a SubRip file](/captions/import-captions/).
1043	
1044	| Setting | Value |
1045	| --- | --- |
1046	| Typeface | Source Sans 3 Regular |
1047	| Size | 3.5% of the canvas's shorter side |
1048	| Alignment | Centred |
1049	| Colour | White, unless a speaker colour applies |
1050	| Backdrop | Black at 60%, with 12 px of padding and 8 px corners |
1051	| Wraps at | 80% of the canvas width |
1052	| Position on a wide or square canvas | The box is centred 38% of the frame height below the middle |
1053	| Position on a canvas taller than wide | The box is centred a quarter of the frame height below the middle |
1054	
1055	On a 1920 × 1080 canvas that's 38 px text that wraps at 1,536 px. On a 1080 × 1920 canvas it's the same 38 px text, wrapping at 864 px. A canvas taller than wide, such as 9:16 or 4:5, also puts the box higher in the frame.
1056	
1057	A narrow canvas can wrap a cue past two lines, because the wrap happens inside the box after the cue is built. On a canvas taller than wide, Frame Job counts these and tells you once the captions are placed:
1058	
1059	> 3 captions wrap to more than two lines on this canvas.
1060	
1061	After generating, this appears on the sheet, which stays open with **Close**. After importing, it's an alert. The captions are placed either way.
1062	
1063	## Good to know
1064	
1065	- An imported SubRip file keeps its own line breaks and timing. The rules in [The Subtitles style](#the-subtitles-style) only apply to generated cues.
1066	- **Replace:** is greyed out with Subtitles chosen. To swap a word caption track for Subtitles, generate the new track, then [remove the old one](/timeline/manage-tracks/).
1067	- [Re-lay Captions for This Canvas](/captions/re-lay-captions/) keeps a Subtitles track as placed. To re-wrap one for a new canvas, generate it again on that canvas.
1068	- A cue has no word timing, so the [looks](/captions/word-caption-looks/) don't apply. All three boxes are greyed out with Subtitles chosen.
1069	- Subtitles are text in the picture, not a track a player can switch off. To ship a separate file, use [Export Captions…](/captions/export-captions/).
1070	
1071	## With an agent
1072	
1073	`transcribe` makes Subtitles (`style: subtitles`) unless it asks for another style, whatever the sheet last chose. See [`transcribe`](/mcp/tools-captions/#transcribe).
1074

1091	The five word styles make the large captions used in shorts and reels, where each word is marked as it's said. For classic two-line cues, use [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/) instead.

1099	## Make word captions
1100	
1101	<Steps>
1102	
1103	1. Choose **File ▸ Generate Captions…**.
1104	
1105	2. Set **Language:**, **Engine:** and **From:**. [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) explains each one.
1106	
1107	3. Set **Style:** to **Highlight**, **Pill**, **Karaoke**, **Build** or **One Word**. The sheet remembers your choice for next time.
1108	
1109	4. Tick any [looks](/captions/word-caption-looks/) you want, and check the [preview](#the-sheets-two-frame-preview).
1110	
1111	5. Choose **Generate**.
1112	
1113	</Steps>
1114	
1115	## Word caption pages
1116	
1117	A word style doesn't make cues. Each clip holds a **page** of words, with each word's timing, and the word being spoken is drawn the way the style says. A page is still an ordinary [text clip](/captions/how-captions-work/), so you can drag, trim and split it.
1118	
1119	All five styles are white with the spoken word marked. Words are marked by their timing only, so there's no keyword emphasis and no emoji.
1120	
1121	The text is 7.5% of the canvas's shorter side, or 12% for One Word. That means a vertical and a horizontal canvas get the same text height: on both 1080 × 1920 and 1920 × 1080 it's 81 px, or 130 px for One Word. Where a style pops the spoken word, the pop takes 0.12 s.
1122	
1123	## The five styles
1124	
1125	### Highlight
1126	
1127	The spoken word turns yellow and pops to 112%, and the other words stay white.
1128	
1129	Montserrat Black with a black outline, in capitals. The box is centred a quarter of the frame height below the middle.
1130	
1131	### Pill
1132	
1133	The spoken word sits on a violet pill, and doesn't change size. [Slide the pill](/captions/word-caption-looks/#slide-the-pill) makes the pill travel between words instead of jumping.
1134	
1135	Montserrat ExtraBold, in capitals. The box is centred a quarter of the frame height below the middle.
1136	
1137	### Karaoke
1138	
1139	Words turn yellow as they're said and stay yellow. Words still to come are white at 55% opacity.
1140	
1141	Montserrat ExtraBold, as written. Karaoke can use up to two lines, and it's the only style that wraps a page of several words. The box is centred 28% of the frame height below the middle.
1142	
1143	### Build
1144	
1145	Words appear one by one. The newest is yellow and pops to 115%, and the ones before it are white.
1146	
1147	Anton with a black outline, in capitals. The box is centred a quarter of the frame height below the middle.
1148	
1149	### One Word
1150	
1151	One large word at a time, white, popping to 120%. Every page holds one word.
1152	
1153	Bebas Neue with a black outline, in capitals. The box is centred 18% of the frame height below the middle.
1154	
1155	## Bundled typefaces
1156	
1157	Montserrat Black, Montserrat ExtraBold, Anton and Bebas Neue ship inside the app under the SIL Open Font License, so there's nothing to install.
1158	
1159	## Pages are filled to their measured width
1160	
1161	A page holds as many words as fit, not a set number. Frame Job measures each page in its style's typeface, size, case and outline on your canvas, and fills it up to 86% of the canvas width, on one line. Karaoke can use two lines, and One Word always holds one word.
1162	
1163	So the same speech makes shorter pages on a 9:16 canvas than on a 16:9 one. On a 1080 × 1920 canvas a page can be about 929 px wide. If you change the canvas size later, [Re-lay Captions for This Canvas](/captions/re-lay-captions/) pages them again.
1164	
1165	When a page ends because the width ran out, Frame Job can move its last word onto the next page if the two then come closer in width. That stops a sentence ending on one word alone.
1166	
1167	## Where a page breaks
1168	
1169	A page ends early at any of these:
1170	
1171	- a pause of 0.25 s or more between two words
1172	- a word ending in `.` `?` `!` or `…`
1173	- 3 seconds on screen, up to the end of the page's last word
1174	- a change of speaker, when [**Speakers:**](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/) is ticked
1175	
1176	When the width runs out within two words of a comma, semicolon or colon, the break moves back to that mark. It only does this when the page is already at least half full and the words that move still fit on the next page.
1177	
1178	On-device words rarely carry a pause, so pages from **On this Mac** break at pauses less often than pages from AssemblyAI.
1179	
1180	## A word too wide for the frame
1181	
1182	A word too wide for a page gets a page of its own and shrinks in 5% steps, down to 80% of the style's size, until it fits. If it's still too wide at 80%, it stays at that size and wraps.
1183	
1184	## How long a page stays up
1185	
1186	A page stays up 0.5 s after its last word, and the row is empty until the next page. If the next page starts sooner than that, the page runs right up to it, so the row doesn't blink between pages.
1187	
1188	Pages never run past the end of the clip they came from.
1189	
1190	## The sheet's two-frame preview
1191	
1192	The preview under the looks shows a sample page, drawn the way the canvas draws it and paged for this canvas's proportions. It shows you how the style looks, not how big it will be, because each frame is scaled to fit the strip.
1193	
1194	| What you see | What it means |
1195	| --- | --- |
1196	| Two frames | A word style, with the first word active in the top frame and the second word in the bottom one. A page of one word shows that word in both. |
1197	| One frame | Subtitles. |
1198	| The sample words | The first words of the first clip's kept AssemblyAI transcript when there is one, otherwise "This is how it looks". |
1199	| A half-filled word | **Fill words as spoken** is ticked. |
1200	| A pill between two words | **Slide the pill** is ticked. It shows in the second frame. |
1201	
1202	**Dim in pauses** isn't previewed.
1203	
1204	## Good to know
1205	
1206	- A style is set when the captions are generated, and you can't switch it on a placed track. To change it, see [Restyle a caption track](/captions/restyle-captions/).
1207	- The capitals are applied when a page is drawn, so the words stay as written in the **Content** box and in an [exported caption file](/captions/export-captions/). To show a page as written, untick **UPPERCASE**. See [Edit captions](/captions/edit-captions/).
1208	- [Text reveals](/text-and-shapes/text-reveal/) don't apply to a timed page.
1209	- The [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/) style is the first choice in the **Style:** pop-up, and it works differently: two-line cues with no word timing.
1210	
1211	## With an agent
1212	
1213	`transcribe` makes word captions when it asks for a word style: `highlight`, `pill`, `karaoke`, `build` or `one_word`. It never uses the style the sheet last chose. See [`transcribe`](/mcp/tools-captions/#transcribe).
1214

1228	---
1229	
1230	
1231	Looks add movement to a [word style](/captions/word-caption-styles/)'s pages: a pill that slides between words, a word that fills as it's said, and a page that dims when nobody's talking.
1232	
1233	<AtAGlance
1234	  menu="File ▸ Generate Captions…"
1235	  where="The Generate Captions sheet, under Style:"
1236	  tools={['transcribe', 'set_text']}
1237	/>
1238	
1239	## Three looks for word captions
1240	
1241	<Steps>
1242	
1243	1. Choose **File ▸ Generate Captions…**, and set **Language:**, **Engine:** and **From:** as [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) explains.
1244	
1245	2. Set **Style:** to a [word style](/captions/word-caption-styles/).
1246	
1247	3. Tick the looks you want under the **Style:** pop-up.
1248	
1249	4. Choose **Generate**.
1250	
1251	</Steps>
1252	
1253	Each look works with some styles and not others:
1254	
1255	| Look | Highlight | Pill | Karaoke | Build | One Word |
1256	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
1257	| **Slide the pill** | | Yes | | | |
1258	| **Fill words as spoken** | Yes | | Yes | Yes | |
1259	| **Dim in pauses** | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
1260	
1261	A box that doesn't apply to the chosen style is greyed out and does nothing, but it keeps its tick for when you switch back. With **Subtitles** chosen, all three are greyed out.
1262	
1263	Each box is off until you tick it, and the sheet remembers each one between runs.
1264	
1265	A look changes how a word is drawn, never a letter or the size of the page. Ticking one doesn't change where pages break.
1266	
1267	Looks are set when the captions are generated, like the style. To change them on a placed track, [generate again with Replace](/captions/restyle-captions/#restyle-by-generating-again).
1268	
1269	## Slide the pill
1270	
1271	The pill slides from the previous word to the one being said, instead of jumping. The slide takes 0.2 s, or less when the next word starts sooner, so the pill has always arrived before it has to leave. The first word on a page has nothing to slide from, so the pill starts there.
1272	
1273	This works with **Pill**, the only style that has one.
1274	
1275	## Fill words as spoken
1276	
1277	The word being said fills from left to right as it's spoken. The fill runs from the word's start to its end, and takes 0.6 s at most, so a long word finishes filling before it's finished being said.
1278	
1279	| Style | The part already said | The rest of the word |
1280	| --- | --- | --- |
1281	| **Highlight** | Yellow | White |
1282	| **Karaoke** | Yellow | White at 55% opacity |
1283	| **Build** | Yellow | Not drawn yet |
1284	
1285	**Pill** and **One Word** can't use this look, because their spoken word is the same colour on both sides of the fill.
1286	
1287	## Dim in pauses
1288	
1289	The page fades to half opacity during a pause of 0.25 s or more, then comes back before the next word. Each fade takes 0.1 s, and the words and the pill fade together. It works with all five word styles.
1290	
1291	The page also dims at either end of a caption, when the wait there is 0.25 s or more:
1292	
1293	- before the first word. The page opens dim, with no fade.
1294	- after the last word, until the caption ends.
1295	
1296	A pause of 0.25 s also [ends a page](/captions/word-caption-styles/#where-a-page-breaks), so on a generated track you'll mostly see the dim at the end of a page, after its last word.
1297	
1298	With **On this Mac** chosen and a word style selected, a note under the boxes reads "On-device words rarely carry a pause; this shows mostly with AssemblyAI."
1299	
1300	The sheet's [preview](/captions/word-caption-styles/#the-sheets-two-frame-preview) doesn't show this look.
1301	
1302	## Word colours
1303	
1304	The inspector has no section for a page's word colours, pop size or pill. Nothing in the Clip tab changes the yellow, the violet or how far the word pops.
1305	
1306	To change them, generate again with a [different style](/captions/restyle-captions/#restyle-by-generating-again), or [have an agent do it](#with-an-agent).
1307	
1308	The **Color** row under **Text ▸ Style** still works on the words drawn in the text's own colour. That's the white words in **Highlight** and **Build**, and every word in **Pill** and **One Word**. It leaves the yellow alone, and it changes nothing in **Karaoke**, which sets all its own colours.
1309	
1310	## With an agent
1311	
1312	An agent can do two things here that the sheet can't.
1313	
1314	It can change a placed page's word style with `set_text`. That covers highlighting or building word by word, the colours of the spoken word and of the words before and after it, a pop from 100% to 150%, the pill's colour, padding and corners, whether the pill slides, whether the word fills, and how far the page dims, from none to fully invisible. The sheet's dim is always half. A page changed this way is no longer one of the styles Frame Job makes, so [Re-lay Captions](/captions/re-lay-captions/#tracks-kept-as-placed) keeps its track as placed. See [Word style](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/#word-style).
1315	
1316	It can also ask for looks with `transcribe`, through `slide`, `fill` and `dim`, but each one is off unless it asks, never what the sheet last chose. Frame Job won't add a look to a style it wouldn't show on, or to captions it isn't placing. When it gives any of the three and the captions are placed, the result lists the looks that were on. See [Caption looks](/mcp/tools-captions/#caption-looks).

1326	######## captions/restyle-captions
1327	---
1328	title: Restyle a caption track
1329	description: Switch a caption track to another word style or look by generating it again, or change the font and backdrop of a run of captions in the inspector.
1330	---
1331	
1332	
1333	There are two ways to restyle captions, depending on what you want to change. A word style and its looks are set when the captions are generated, so changing those means generating again. Font, outline and backdrop are ordinary text settings, which you can change on a run of captions in the inspector.
1334	
1335	<AtAGlance
1336	  menu="File ▸ Generate Captions…"
1337	  where={['The Generate Captions sheet ▸ Replace:', 'Clip tab ▸ Text']}
1338	  tools={['transcribe', 'set_text']}
1339	/>
1340	
1341	## Restyle by generating again
1342	
1343	<Steps>
1344	
1345	1. Choose **File ▸ Generate Captions…** and set **From:** to the same clips.
1346	
1347	2. Set **Style:** to the new word style and tick any [looks](/captions/word-caption-looks/).
1348	
1349	3. Tick **Replace: existing captions**. The line under it names each track it will remove, with its caption count, for example "Replaces “Captions” (12 captions)."
1350	
1351	4. Choose **Generate**.
1352	
1353	</Steps>
1354	
1355	The old tracks are removed and the new one takes their place at the front of the stack, all in one undo step, **Generate Captions**. The new track takes the first free name, so a lone **Captions** track is replaced by another called **Captions**.
1356	
1357	What it costs depends on the engine:
1358	
1359	- **AssemblyAI:** the kept transcript is reused whatever style you ask for, so nothing is uploaded and nothing is billed. That holds while the language, **Speakers:** and **Vocabulary:** match the transcript and **Transcribe again:** stays unticked. See [Transcribe with AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/).
1360	- **On this Mac:** the audio is recognised again. It's free, but it takes the time again.
1361	
1362	:::caution
1363	New pages are made from the transcript, not from the old track. Words you corrected, pages you split or trimmed, and anything you restyled by hand go with the old track. To page a track again and keep your corrections, use [Re-lay Captions](/captions/re-lay-captions/) instead.
1364	:::
1365	
1366	## Which tracks Replace may remove
1367	
1368	**Replace:** is available only for a word style, and only when there's a track it may replace. It's greyed out with Subtitles chosen. When it isn't available, it's unticked and the line under it is hidden.
1369	
1370	A track qualifies when:
1371	
1372	- it's named **Captions** or **Captions N**, such as **Captions 2**. A track you renamed doesn't qualify.
1373	- it holds at least one clip, and only text clips.
1374	- every one of those clips overlaps a clip being transcribed.
1375	
1376	The last rule is about the whole track. If even one caption on it sits outside what **From:** covers, the track is left alone and **Replace:** won't list it. Choosing a wider **From:** can bring it in.
1377	
1378	The old track's style doesn't matter, so **Replace:** also swaps out a Subtitles track or an [imported](/captions/import-captions/) one that meets these rules.
1379	
1380	## Change a run of captions together
1381	
1382	To change the font, outline or backdrop and leave the word style alone, select the captions and use the inspector.
1383	
1384	<Steps>
1385	
1386	1. [Select the captions](/timeline/selecting-clips/) on the timeline.
1387	
1388	2. Open the **Clip** tab and its **Text** sub-tab.
1389	
1390	3. Change what you need under [**Font**, **Style**](/text-and-shapes/text-style/), [**Outline**, **Backdrop**](/text-and-shapes/text-outline-and-backdrop/) or [**Box**](/text-and-shapes/text-box/).
1391	
1392	</Steps>
1393	
1394	Each page keeps its own words and word timing. Its word style stays too: the highlight colour, the pop and the pill only change by generating again, or through an agent. See [Word colours](/captions/word-caption-looks/#word-colours).
1395	
1396	:::note
1397	A change of typeface on a word caption page, which a text preset also makes, means Re-lay Captions no longer recognises its track and [keeps it as placed](/captions/re-lay-captions/#tracks-kept-as-placed).
1398	:::
1399	
1400	## Good to know
1401	
1402	- **Replace:** always opens unticked. The sheet doesn't remember it.
1403	- A hidden or locked caption track is replaced like any other, and the new track is visible and unlocked.
1404	- If you cancel a run, nothing is placed and the old tracks stay.
1405	- If one file can't be transcribed, the captions from the other files are still placed and the old tracks still go, so the captions over that file's clips are lost. Undo brings them back.
1406	- To go from a word style back to Subtitles, generate the Subtitles track, then [remove the old one](/timeline/manage-tracks/). **Replace:** isn't available for that.
1407	- With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, the sheet works on that nest's tracks.
1408	
1409	## With an agent
1410	
1411	[`transcribe`](/mcp/tools-captions/#restyle-captions) restyles the same way with `replace`, as long as it asks for a word style and places the captions. An agent can also change a placed page's word style directly with [`set_text`](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/#word-style), which keeps your corrected words. See [Word colours](/captions/word-caption-looks/#with-an-agent).

1422	######## captions/re-lay-captions
1423	---
1424	title: Re-lay captions for a canvas
1425	description: Page word captions again after a canvas size change, keeping every word you corrected, and find out why a track was left as it was.
1426	---
1427	
1428	
1429	[Word captions](/captions/word-caption-styles/#word-caption-pages) are split into pages that fit the canvas they were made on, so a narrower canvas can leave them too wide. Re-lay Captions splits them into pages again for the new width, from the words they already hold.
1430	
1431	<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ Re-lay Captions for This Canvas" tools="relay_captions" />
1432	
1433	## Re-lay Captions for This Canvas
1434	
1435	<Steps>
1436	
1437	1. [Change the canvas size](/projects/canvas-size/) on the Document tab.
1438	
1439	2. Choose **File ▸ Re-lay Captions for This Canvas**. It has no keyboard shortcut and no options.
1440	
1441	3. If a sheet appears, read which tracks were [kept as placed](#tracks-kept-as-placed) and why.
1442	
1443	</Steps>
1444	
1445	Frame Job looks at every track named **Captions** or **Captions N** that holds only text clips. A track whose pages are all in one of the five [word styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/), with the same [looks](/captions/word-caption-looks/), is paged again from the words its pages hold. Nothing is transcribed again, so nothing is uploaded or billed.
1446	
1447	The whole re-lay is one undo step, **Re-lay Captions**.
1448	
1449	## What a re-lay keeps
1450	
1451	Every correction you typed is kept, because the new pages are made from the words on the old ones.
1452	
1453	Each page is paged again inside its own clip, and the new pages take the old track's place:
1454	
1455	- A page you split, trimmed or moved keeps its words where they are.
1456	- Pages are never merged across clips. A re-lay can split a page that's too wide for the new canvas, but a wider canvas won't join short pages together.
1457	- Words cut off by a trim stay cut off.
1458	- The new pages go on a track with the same name, in the same place in the track stack, hidden and locked if the old one was.
1459	
1460	The new pages are drawn fresh from the style, so any other change you made to a page goes. That includes a colour, an outline, a size, a position, or an unticked **UPPERCASE**.
1461	
1462	## Tracks kept as placed
1463	
1464	A track that can't be re-laid stays exactly as it was. A sheet after the edit names each one and why, under a first line that reads "Re-laid 2 caption tracks for this canvas." or "No caption track was re-laid."
1465	
1466	Each track gets a line like this:
1467	
1468	> Caption track "Captions 2" is kept as placed: it holds a page with no word timings.
1469	
1470	| The reason | What it means |
1471	| --- | --- |
1472	| it is a matte track | The track is a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/). |
1473	| it holds a page with no word timings | It's a [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/) or imported track, or a page lost its timing because you [changed its number of words](/captions/edit-captions/). |
1474	| it holds a page none of whose words starts inside it | A trim or split left a page with no word that begins on it. |
1475	| it holds a page in a style Frame Job does not make | You changed a page's font, or an agent changed its word style. |
1476	| its pages are in more than one style | Pages on the track differ in style or looks, for example after you moved some from another track. |
1477	| *N* captions is more than this project has room for | The new pages would take the project past its limit of 4,096 clips. The sentence says how many more would fit. |
1478	
1479	No sheet appears when every track was re-laid.
1480	
1481	To re-wrap a Subtitles track, or a track that lost its timing, generate it again on the new canvas. See [Restyle a caption track](/captions/restyle-captions/).
1482	
1483	## When it is available, and inside a nest
1484	
1485	The item is greyed out when:
1486	
1487	- there's no caption track it can re-lay
1488	- a sheet is open
1489	- a recording is running
1490	
1491	So if every caption track is ruled out by a reason in the table above, other than the project's clip limit, the item is greyed out and no sheet tells you why.
1492	
1493	Inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), it works on the nest's tracks at the nest's size.
1494	
1495	**File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** does the same for the vertical copy. See [What Make Vertical changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/).
1496	
1497	## Good to know
1498	
1499	- A track with any other name isn't looked at, and the sheet doesn't mention it. Neither is a track that holds a clip other than text.
1500	- The item doesn't check whether the canvas changed. Choosing it on the same canvas pages the track again, which still drops the hand changes listed in [What a re-lay keeps](#what-a-re-lay-keeps). Undo brings them back.
1501	
1502	## With an agent
1503	
1504	`relay_captions` does the same in the timeline or nest that's open, usually after `set_canvas` changes the size. It takes no arguments, and its result lists the tracks it re-laid and each kept track with its reason. When nothing can be re-laid, the call fails with those reasons, so an agent can tell you why the menu item is greyed out. See [`relay_captions`](/mcp/tools-captions/#relay_captions).
1505

1515	######## captions/edit-captions
1516	---
1517	title: "Edit captions"
1518	description: "Change a caption's words, case, look, position and timing, and see which edits keep a word caption's word-by-word timing."
1519	---
1520	
1521	
1522	A caption is an ordinary text clip, so you edit it the way you edit any text clip. The one thing to watch is word captions. Each of their clips is a **page** of words, with every word timed to the speech. Most edits keep that timing, and a few drop it.
1523	
1524	<AtAGlance
1525	  where={['Clip tab ▸ Text sections', 'Double-click a page on the canvas', 'The timeline']}
1526	  tools="set_text"
1527	/>
1528	
1529	## Edit captions in the Text sections
1530	
1531	Select a caption and open the **Clip** tab. The **Text** sections are **Content**, **Font**, **Style**, **Outline**, **Backdrop**, **Box**, **Reveal** and **Presets**, and they work as they do for any [text clip](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/).
1532	
1533	Select several captions to change them together. That's the quick way to set a font or a colour across a whole run. Take care with **Content**, though: what you type there replaces the text of every selected caption.
1534	
1535	To move a caption on the screen, drag it on the canvas or use the **Transform** section. To change when it shows, use the timeline, as [below](#trimming-splitting-and-moving-a-page). The **Presets** buttons set position as well as look.
1536	
1537	## Change the words on a page
1538	
1539	Type in the **Content** box, or double-click the page on the canvas and [type there](/text-and-shapes/edit-text-on-canvas/). The same rule holds in both places:
1540	
1541	| You change | What happens to the timing |
1542	| --- | --- |
1543	| The text, keeping the same number of words | Every word keeps its timing. Fixing a misheard word is safe. |
1544	| The number of words | The page loses its timing and shows plainly, with no word-by-word effect. |
1545	
1546	Words are counted by the spaces between them, so turning "gonna" into "going to" changes the count.
1547	
1548	A page that has lost its timing says **Not timed — regenerate to time it again** in the **Content** section. To time it again, [generate the captions again](/captions/restyle-captions/#restyle-by-generating-again). The new pages come from the speech, not from the old track, so your corrections, splits, trims and hand styling on that track go too.
1549	
1550	## Case on a word page
1551	
1552	The capitals on a word caption come from its style, through the **UPPERCASE** box in the **Style** section. Untick it to show a page as written.
1553	
1554	Case is applied when the page is drawn, so the **Content** box always shows the words as written, however the page looks. Changing case never drops the word timing.
1555	
1556	## Trimming, splitting and moving a page
1557	
1558	Trim, split and drag a page on the timeline with the usual tools. All three are safe for word timing:
1559	
1560	- **Trim** changes when the page is on screen. Each word stays on the speech it times, and the page's text doesn't change.
1561	- **Split** gives you two clips that play as the one page did. Both keep the page's words, each word still on its speech.
1562	- **Dragging** a page moves its words with it, so they stay in step with the page, not with the speech under it.
1563	
1564	## Reveals do not apply to a timed page
1565	
1566	The text reveals (**Typewriter**, **Word Fade** and **Line Rise**) don't work on a word caption page. The rows in the **Reveal** section are greyed, and the section says **Word style wins; the reveal does not apply.**
1567	
1568	That's true of any page with a word style, including one that has lost its timing.
1569	
1570	## Change a page's word style
1571	
1572	No inspector section sets a word style's highlight colour, pop scale or pill colour. To change them, [generate the captions again](/captions/restyle-captions/#restyle-by-generating-again) with a different style, or ask an agent.
1573	
1574	## Newly revealed speech stays uncaptioned
1575	
1576	When a speed-up or a ramp makes a clip play further into its file, the new part gets no captions until you choose **File ▸ Generate Captions…** again. [Captions follow a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/) explains how the captions you already have move.
1577	
1578	## Word timings for agents
1579	
1580	An agent can do two things here that the inspector can't: rewrite a page's word timings, and change its word style, both with `set_text`. Frame Job won't take a set of timings that doesn't have exactly one timing for each word of the page, so a change to the number of words has to clear the timings in the same call. Word timings can't be animated with an action. See [Word timings and word style](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/#word-timings-and-word-style).
1581	
1582	## Good to know
1583	
1584	- With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected on a page, a **Content** edit goes to that action and the page keeps its timing. Where the action's text has a different number of words from the page, the page shows plainly.
1585	- A split page is two text clips, so an [exported caption file](/captions/export-captions/) has two cues with the same words.
1586	- Frame Job won't run [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/) over a caption page with timed words. Move the range off the page first.
1587

1598	######## captions/export-captions
1599	---
1600	title: "Export captions"
1601	description: "Write a track of captions out as a SubRip or WebVTT file to ship beside your movie, without changing the project."
1602	---
1603	
1604	
1605	Export Captions writes one track of captions out as a separate subtitle file, for a platform or player that takes one. Burned-in captions need none of this: they're part of the picture in any [movie you export](/export/export-sheet/).
1606	
1607	<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ Export Captions…" tools="export_captions" />
1608	
1609	## Export captions
1610	
1611	<Steps>
1612	
1613	1. Choose **File ▸ Export Captions…**. It has no keyboard shortcut, and it's greyed out until some track holds only text clips, with caption text on at least one of them.
1614	
1615	2. In the save panel, choose the [**Track**](#track) and the [**Format**](#format-subrip-or-webvtt). The name starts as your project's name with `.srt` on the end.
1616	
1617	3. Choose **Save**.
1618	
1619	</Steps>
1620	
1621	Exporting changes nothing in the project, so there's no undo step. If the file can't be written, an alert says why.
1622	
1623	## Track
1624	
1625	The **Track** pop-up lists the tracks you can write, front-most first, with the front-most chosen. Each row reads like "Captions — 12 cues (track 4)". The pop-up is greyed when there's only one to choose.
1626	
1627	Nothing marks a track as a caption track, so any track made only of text clips is listed, a titles track included. A track with any other kind of clip on it isn't listed, and neither is one whose text clips are all empty.
1628	
1629	With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, the list shows that nest's tracks.
1630	
1631	## Format: SubRip or WebVTT
1632	
1633	The **Format** pop-up offers **SubRip (.srt)**, the default, and **WebVTT (.vtt)**. Choose whichever your player or platform asks for. Changing it changes the extension in the name field and keeps the name you've typed.
1634	
1635	The words and times are the same in both. The files differ like this:
1636	
1637	| | SubRip | WebVTT |
1638	| --- | --- | --- |
1639	| First line of the file | The first cue | `WEBVTT` |
1640	| A number above each cue | Yes | No |
1641	| Timestamps | `00:00:04,133` | `00:00:04.133` |
1642	| `&`, `<` and `>` in the text | Written as they are | Escaped |
1643	
1644	Both use Unix (LF) line endings and end with one newline.
1645	
1646	## One cue per text clip
1647	
1648	Each text clip on the track becomes one cue, at the time and with the words it has now. A caption you dragged exports where you dragged it. Styling plays no part, so restyling a caption doesn't change the file.
1649	
1650	- A caption with no text is left out.
1651	- Line endings become LF. Blank lines inside a caption are removed, and so are spaces at the ends of its lines.
1652	- A word caption track is written one cue per page, with the page's words as written. The style's **UPPERCASE**, the word timings and the styling don't go in the file.
1653	
1654	## Frame-exact round trips
1655	
1656	Export a track and [import it again](/captions/import-captions/), and every cue goes back on the frame it came from, at every ordinary frame rate.
1657	
1658	The file itself may not match the one you first imported, because import moves each time onto a whole frame. At 30 fps, `00:00:04,120` comes back as `00:00:04,133`. A file only comes back byte for byte when its cue times are already on whole frames and a frame lasts a whole number of milliseconds, as it does at 25 or 50 fps.
1659	
1660	## With an agent
1661	
1662	`export_captions` takes a `path`, and can be given a `track` and a `format`. With no `format` it follows the path's `.srt` or `.vtt`, and a `format` you name wins over the extension.
1663	
1664	It never guesses the track. With no track to write, it writes nothing and says so. With more than one and none named, it writes nothing and lists the candidates. A track it writes comes back through `import_captions` with every cue where it was. See [`export_captions`](/mcp/tools-captions/#export_captions).
1665	
1666	## Related

1675	######## captions/transcript-tab
1676	---
1677	title: "The Transcript tab"
1678	description: "Read everything said in your project as text in the inspector, and choose which track and language the words come from."
1679	---
1680	
1681	
1682	The Transcript tab shows what's said in your project as text you can read and click. It's the whole timeline as words, in the order you'd hear them, through every trim, speed change and nest. The spoken word [lights up](/captions/follow-the-transcript/) as the playhead passes it, and you can [cut by deleting words](/captions/delete-words/).
1683	
1684	<AtAGlance
1685	  menu="View ▸ Transcript"
1686	  keys="⌃⌘T"
1687	  where="Inspector ▸ Transcript, between Document and the Assistant"
1688	  tools={['get_timeline_transcript', 'get_transcript']}
1689	  needs="A speech model on this Mac, or an AssemblyAI transcript of the file. No key is needed to read."
1690	/>
1691	
1692	<Shot
1693	  name="11c-transcript-tab.inspector"
1694	  alt="The inspector's Transcript tab, with the Words from and Language pop-ups at the top and the timeline's words below them in paragraphs, each led by its timecode."
1695	/>
1696	
1697	## Open the Transcript
1698	
1699	Choose **View ▸ Transcript** or press <kbd>⌃⌘T</kbd>. The inspector opens if it was hidden, the tab shows, and the text takes the keyboard, so the [transcript keys](/captions/transcript-keys/) work at once. It isn't a toggle: choosing it again leaves the tab showing.
1700	
1701	You can also click **Transcript** in the inspector's tab strip. That shows the tab without giving the text the keyboard, until you click in it.
1702	
1703	The first time you look, the tab may need to read your files, which means transcribing them on this Mac. See [Where the transcript's words come from](/captions/transcript-words/).
1704	
1705	## Every word you would hear
1706	
1707	The tab lists every word you'd hear if the timeline played, in order. That takes in clips on every track, and clips inside nests where they play.
1708	
1709	It leaves out what you wouldn't hear: muted tracks, clips [soloed out](/audio/mute-and-solo/), clips turned down to silence and clips with their audio switched off.
1710	
1711	With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open (<kbd>⌘↓</kbd>), the tab shows only what's inside it.
1712	
1713	## Paragraphs and timecodes
1714	
1715	The words come in paragraphs, each with its timecode above it. A new paragraph starts when:
1716	
1717	- the words move to another track
1718	- the speaker changes, which only a transcript from AssemblyAI can tell
1719	- there are 1.5 seconds or more between two clips' words on one track
1720	- the speaker pauses for 1.5 seconds or more inside a clip
1721	
1722	A change of speaker starts a paragraph, and the tab doesn't print a speaker's name.
1723	
1724	Some words show faint, and a pause over a second can show as a grey length such as "[2.4 s]". Those are about cutting. See [Cut by deleting words](/captions/delete-words/) and [Shorten a pause](/captions/shorten-pauses/).
1725	
1726	## The bar
1727	
1728	A bar sits above the text and stays put while the text scrolls. It holds the two pop-ups, then short notes on what the tab is doing and anything it couldn't read.
1729	
1730	**Words from** and **Language** belong to the window. They stay while it's open, whichever tab you look at, and they aren't saved with the project.
1731	
1732	### Words from
1733	
1734	**Words from** chooses whose words to show: **All tracks**, the default, or one track by name. With one track chosen, the tab shows only the words on it, and reads only the files with a clip on it. If that track goes away, the tab goes back to **All tracks**.
1735	
1736	### Language
1737	
1738	**Language** chooses the language files are read in on this Mac.
1739	
1740	**Automatic** is your Mac's language, shown in brackets as a code such as `en-US`. If you have no speech model for it, Automatic uses another form of the same language, or failing that the first language you have. Below it is every language your Mac has a speech model for. The pop-up is disabled when there are none.
1741	
1742	Choosing a language reads the files again in that language. The earlier reading is kept too, so switching back is immediate. A file with an AssemblyAI transcript keeps showing that transcript whichever you choose.
1743	
1744	### Read and Stop
1745	
1746	While a file is being read on this Mac, a note shows its progress, with **Stop** beside it:
1747	
1748	> Reading “interview.mov” on this Mac… 40 % (1 of 2)
1749	
1750	**Stop** leaves the rest of the files unread, and the note changes:
1751	
1752	> Stopped. 2 files not read on this Mac.
1753	
1754	**Read** carries on from there, and so does coming back to the tab after looking at another one. Editing the timeline or changing **Words from** or **Language** doesn't start it again.
1755	
1756	A file you stop part-way isn't kept, so it's read from its start next time. **Stop** ends only the tab's own reading: if an agent is waiting for the same file's words at that moment, its reading goes on.
1757	
1758	## Clips with no words
1759	
1760	A clip that can't give any words is listed under the pop-ups with the reason, such as "clip 12 — its audio is switched off". A clip inside a nest reads "clip 12 in nest Intro — …".
1761	
1762	| The note says | What to do |
1763	| --- | --- |
1764	| its audio is switched off | Turn the clip's audio on. |
1765	| its media has no audio track | Nothing. The file has no sound to read. |
1766	| its media file is missing | [Relink the file](/projects/relink-media/). |
1767	| it plays in reverse, so its speech cannot be transcribed | Turn off [Reverse](/speed/reverse/) to read it. |
1768	
1769	The first three clips are listed. "…and 4 more clips with no words." stands for the rest, and holding the pointer over it lists them.
1770	
1771	## The same speech on two tracks
1772	
1773	When two clips carry the same speech, such as a camera's sound and a separate microphone, a note names the pair:
1774	
1775	> Clips 3 and 7 carry the same speech. Mute one, or switch its audio off, to read it once.
1776	
1777	Both stay in the text until you do. The note appears for clips of different files that overlap for at least 5 seconds, when at least 60% of the words of the clip with fewer words in that overlap also appear in the other, in the same order.
1778	
1779	## Good to know
1780	
1781	- Nothing you do in the tab's bar changes the project, and the words aren't part of your edit.
1782	- The tab has no search.
1783	
1784	## With an agent
1785	
1786	Agents read the same words with `get_timeline_transcript`. It returns the same notes as `notes` and the clips with no words as `no_words`, and its `tracks` and `language` do what **Words from** and **Language** do. See [`get_timeline_transcript`](/mcp/tools-captions/#get_timeline_transcript).
1787
