1797	######## captions/transcript-words
1798	---
1799	title: "Where the transcript's words come from"
1800	description: "How the Transcript tab gets its words, from an AssemblyAI transcript or by reading on this Mac, and what it keeps so the next look is immediate."
1801	---
1802	
1803	
1804	The [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-tab/) needs no setting up. It uses a transcript you already have, or transcribes the file on this Mac the first time you look, which the tab calls reading it. Either way it sends nothing anywhere.
1805	
1806	<AtAGlance
1807	  where="Inspector ▸ Transcript"
1808	  tools={['get_timeline_transcript', 'get_transcript']}
1809	  needs="A speech model on this Mac, for any file with no AssemblyAI transcript."
1810	/>
1811	
1812	## AssemblyAI first, otherwise this Mac
1813	
1814	For each file, the tab takes the first of these it finds:
1815	
1816	1. **An AssemblyAI transcript.** You have one if you've used [**File ▸ Generate Captions…** with AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/) or [**Remove Filler Words**](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/) on the file. Using it needs no key.
1817	2. **A reading on this Mac.** Otherwise the tab transcribes the file the first time you look, in your Mac's language unless you [choose another](/captions/transcript-tab/#language).
1818	
1819	Reading on this Mac is quick: about 0.7 seconds a minute of speech on an M2 Max, so an hour takes well under a minute. Playback keeps running while it reads.
1820	
1821	The tab never makes a network request, whichever source it uses.
1822	
1823	## One file at a time, playhead first
1824	
1825	Files are read one at a time, starting with the one under the playhead. Each file's words appear as soon as it's done, without waiting for the rest.
1826	
1827	If you switch to another tab, the reading stops, and it picks up when you come back. To stop it yourself, use [**Stop**](/captions/transcript-tab/#read-and-stop).
1828	
1829	## Kept per file and language
1830	
1831	What this Mac heard is kept in the project's [cache](/reference/framejob-package/#cache), one reading for each file and language, so the next look is immediate.
1832	
1833	Each file is read whole, once. Trimming a clip, adding another clip of the same file or changing its speed doesn't read it again.
1834	
1835	A reading is used only while the file and the macOS version are the same. If either changes, or you choose another language, the file is read again.
1836	
1837	These readings are only for the transcript. [Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) and [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/) never use them.
1838	
1839	## When no speech model is installed
1840	
1841	If your Mac has no speech model, the tab says:
1842	
1843	> This Mac has no speech model installed. Choose File ▸ Generate Captions…, pick a language and press Download.
1844	
1845	Do that, then come back to the tab. A file with an AssemblyAI transcript shows its words in the meantime.
1846	
1847	A file this Mac can't read is named in the same place, and the tab carries on with the others. It tries that file again when you next come back to the tab.
1848	
1849	## Ramped clips and following edits
1850	
1851	Words are placed through a clip's speed, including a [ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/), so a word's time matches what plays on the timeline.
1852	
1853	Editing the timeline updates the text right away, and the words you were reading stay where they were. During a drag, the text updates when you let go.
1854	
1855	## With an agent
1856	
1857	An agent reads these words with `get_timeline_transcript`, or one clip's with `get_transcript`. When it reads a file on this Mac, the tab's **Stop** leaves that reading running. The Assistant's own **Stop** ends it, unless the tab is reading that file too, and nothing is saved from a stopped reading. See [`get_timeline_transcript`](/mcp/tools-captions/#get_timeline_transcript) and [`get_transcript`](/mcp/tools-captions/#get_transcript).

1868	---
1869	title: "Follow along and jump"
1870	description: "Watch the spoken word light up as the video plays, and use the transcript to move around the timeline."
1871	---
1872	
1873	
1874	The [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-tab/) stays in step with the playhead, and works the other way too: click the text and the playhead goes there. Use it to find a moment by what was said, instead of scrubbing for it.
1875	
1876	<AtAGlance
1877	  menu="View ▸ Transcript"
1878	  keys="⌃⌘T"
1879	  where="Inspector ▸ Transcript"
1880	  tools={['get_timeline_transcript', 'set_playhead']}
1881	/>
1882	
1883	## The word being spoken
1884	
1885	While the video plays, the word being spoken is highlighted. It stays lit through the pause after it, until the next word starts. Before the first word, nothing is lit.
1886	
1887	The highlight follows the playhead when you're paused too, so moving the playhead by hand lights the word there.
1888	
1889	## The text scrolls with playback
1890	
1891	During playback the text scrolls to keep the spoken word in view.
1892	
1893	If you scroll the text yourself, it stays where you put it for three seconds before it follows again. With playback paused, the text doesn't scroll on its own.
1894	
1895	## Click a word to jump
1896	
1897	Click a word to move the playhead to it and select it. The playhead lands on a whole frame. If the video is playing, it keeps playing from there.
1898	
1899	The selected word becomes the timeline's in/out range, so clicking a word replaces any range you've set. See [Cut by deleting words](/captions/delete-words/).
1900	
1901	## Click a timecode to jump
1902	
1903	Click a paragraph's timecode to move the playhead to the start of that paragraph. Unlike a click on a word, this doesn't change the selection.
1904	
1905	## A selected clip scrolls to its words
1906	
1907	Click a clip that's already selected, on the timeline or the canvas, while the Transcript shows. The tab stays, and the clip's first word scrolls to the top. The playhead doesn't move.
1908	
1909	The click that selects a clip doesn't bring its words up, so click it a second time. Leave a moment between the clicks: a double-click on the timeline renames the clip, or opens a nest.
1910	
1911	For a nest clip, that's the first word inside the nest. A clip with no words in the tab scrolls nothing.
1912	
1913	## Loop plays the selected words
1914	
1915	Whatever you select in the text becomes the in/out range, so [Loop](/timeline/loop/) can play it. Use it to hear a cut before you make it.
1916	
1917	<Steps>
1918	
1919	1. Select the words: drag across them, or click the first and <kbd>⇧</kbd>-click the last.
1920	
1921	2. Turn on **Loop**, the repeat button in the toolbar.
1922	
1923	3. Press <kbd>Space</kbd>.
1924	
1925	</Steps>
1926	
1927	Change the selection and the next pass plays the new range. <kbd>⎋</kbd> clears the selection and the range with it, and Loop then goes round the whole timeline.
1928	
1929	## With an agent
1930	
1931	[`get_timeline_transcript`](/mcp/tools-captions/#get_timeline_transcript) gives each word's time on the timeline, and [`set_playhead`](/mcp/tools-view-state/#set_playhead) moves the playhead there.

1941	######## captions/delete-words
1942	---
1943	title: "Cut by deleting words"
1944	description: Select words in the Transcript tab and delete them, taking the picture and sound under them out of the timeline and closing the gap.
1945	---
1946	
1947	
1948	Editing a spoken video can work like editing text. Select words in the Transcript tab, press <kbd>⌫</kbd>, and the words and everything under them come out of the timeline, with the gap closed.
1949	
1950	<AtAGlance
1951	  menu={['Edit ▸ Delete', 'Edit ▸ Ripple Delete']}
1952	  keys={['⌫', '⌦', '⌘⌫']}
1953	  where="Inspector ▸ Transcript"
1954	  tools={['get_timeline_transcript', 'get_transcript', 'ripple_delete_ranges', 'set_range']}
1955	  needs="Words in the Transcript tab, read on this Mac or from an AssemblyAI transcript. Cutting them uploads nothing."
1956	/>
1957	
1958	## Delete words
1959	
1960	<Steps>
1961	
1962	1. Choose **View ▸ Transcript** (<kbd>⌃⌘T</kbd>). The Transcript tab opens and its text takes the keyboard. The first time you look, the tab has to [read the file](/captions/transcript-words/), so the words can take a moment to appear.
1963	
1964	2. [Select the words](#select-words) you want gone.
1965	
1966	3. Look at what's shaded on the timeline. That's exactly what will go. To hear it first, turn on [Loop](/timeline/loop/), which plays the shaded range.
1967	
1968	4. Press <kbd>⌫</kbd>.
1969	
1970	</Steps>
1971	
1972	The words and the sound under them come out of every unlocked track and the gap closes, as one undo step named **Delete Words**. The range clears and the playhead lands where the cut was.
1973	
1974	<kbd>⌦</kbd>, <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd>, **Edit ▸ Delete** and **Edit ▸ Ripple Delete** all do the same thing here. On the timeline, <kbd>⌫</kbd> [leaves a gap](/editing/delete-clips/). In the transcript it closes the gap, the way deleting text does.
1975	
1976	Deleting words one at a time gives the same result as deleting them together, unless a pause of more than a second lies between them. See [where a word cut falls](#where-a-word-cut-falls).
1977	
1978	:::caution
1979	These keys cut words only while the transcript text has the keyboard. If it doesn't, <kbd>⌫</kbd> does what it does on the timeline: with no clip selected, it lifts the shaded range and leaves a gap. Choose **View ▸ Transcript** first to give the text the keyboard. A click on a word would replace your selection.
1980	:::
1981	
1982	## Select words
1983	
1984	| To | Do this |
1985	| --- | --- |
1986	| Select one word | Click it. The playhead moves to it too. |
1987	| Select a run of words | Drag across them. The text scrolls as you go, and a drag selects words only, never a pause. |
1988	| Extend the selection | <kbd>⇧</kbd>-click a word, or press <kbd>⇧</kbd> with an arrow. Neither moves the playhead. |
1989	| Select every word | Press <kbd>⌘A</kbd>. |
1990	| Clear the selection | Press <kbd>⎋</kbd>. |
1991	
1992	[Transcript keys](/captions/transcript-keys/) has every key the text takes.
1993	
1994	## The selection becomes the range
1995	
1996	Whatever you select becomes the timeline's [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/), replacing any range you had, so the timeline shades exactly what will go. With the range set you can [loop](/timeline/loop/) or [export](/export/range/) only those words.
1997	
1998	The selection can grow as it does this. It widens over any word the cut would cut into, so what's highlighted is what the cut takes. The range lands on the nearest whole frames.
1999	
2000	<kbd>⎋</kbd> clears the selection and the range with it. It clears only a range the selection set: if you've changed the range since, with <kbd>I</kbd>, <kbd>O</kbd> or an agent, the transcript leaves it alone.
2001	
2002	## Where a word cut falls
2003	
2004	A cut runs from where the first word starts to where the next word you keep starts. The pause before the cut stays, and the pause after it goes.
2005	
2006	- **A long pause after the words.** The cut goes no more than one second past the end of the last deleted word, and the rest of the pause stays.
2007	- **Frames.** Both ends land on whole frames, and the end never passes the start of a word that stays.
2008	- **The last word on the timeline.** With no word after it, the cut ends where the word ends.
2009	- **A clip not read yet.** The cut stops at the start of a clip whose words haven't been read.
2010	
2011	## Where a word starts
2012	
2013	When words are [read on this Mac](/captions/transcript-words/), the recogniser puts each word's start early, often well inside the pause before it. So the tab moves each start to where its sound begins. There's nothing for you to do, and this is how it works:
2014	
2015	1. It finds where the voice model, the one [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) uses, first hears speech after the recogniser's start.
2016	2. It then looks for the first hundredth of a second loud enough to be the word: at least −40 dBFS, and 12 dB above the pause's own background noise. The search starts no more than about 0.1 s before the speech, so a click earlier in the pause isn't taken for the word. If nothing is that loud, the start stays where the voice model heard speech.
2017	
2018	A word after a pause therefore starts on its sound, so a cut that ends at that word neither keeps a slice of the pause nor takes the start of the word you keep.
2019	
2020	Both steps use what the project measures when it opens a file. Until the voice model has heard a file, the starts are the recogniser's own. The tab moves them as soon as it has, and keeps your selection.
2021	
2022	Words from an [AssemblyAI transcript](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/), and where any word ends, are left as transcribed.
2023	
2024	## How exact a word cut is
2025	
2026	Word edges come from the transcript itself, so in fast speech a cut can take the very end of the word before it, or leave a sliver of the word you deleted. Play the shaded range with [Loop](/timeline/loop/) before you delete, and undo if the cut sounds wrong.
2027	
2028	## Overlapping words on other tracks
2029	
2030	If a word on another track starts before your selection and runs into it, say two people talking at once, the tab adds that word to the selection first, along with any words between. You see everything the cut takes before you press <kbd>⌫</kbd>.
2031	
2032	A word on another track that starts inside your last selected word isn't added. It's the next word you keep, so the cut ends at its start, and the rest of the deleted word after that point can stay in.
2033	
2034	Only the words the tab shows are added. With **Words from** set to one track, the cut still goes through the other unlocked tracks, and any words it takes there are ones you can't see.
2035	
2036	## Words that can't be cut
2037	
2038	Some words are shown faint, because a cut at them would break something. Hold the pointer over one to read why.
2039	
2040	| Where the word is | What the tab says |
2041	| --- | --- |
2042	| Inside a [nest](/editing/nests/) | "Inside nest *name*: open it (⌘↓) to cut its words." |
2043	| Under a [transition](/motion/transitions/) | "Under a transition: a cut here would leave one clip's tail under its neighbour." |
2044	| On a locked track | "Track *name* is locked: a cut would leave these words in place and move everything after them." |
2045	
2046	A nest or track with no name is given by its number. With a nest open, the tab shows only what's inside it, and a word there is no longer faint for being in that nest.
2047	
2048	You can still click a faint word to move the playhead there, but a selection that holds one can't be deleted. A clip with a [speed ramp](/speed/make-a-ramp/) isn't faint: its words can be cut.
2049	
2050	## When the tab won't cut
2051	
2052	In these cases the tab beeps, keeps your selection and shows the reason at the foot of the inspector, after the word "Refused:". The message stays until the project changes or you click it.
2053	
2054	| Why | What it says |
2055	| --- | --- |
2056	| A selected word is [faint](#words-that-cant-be-cut). | That word's own reason. |
2057	| A locked track has words inside the cut, even a track **Words from** is hiding. A locked track never moves, so its words would fall out of step. | "Track Music is locked and has words in this cut: unlock it to cut here." |
2058	| The cut would pass the project's limit of 4,096 clips while it's being made. Every clip the cut crosses is split first, so a project near the limit can pass it for a moment even if the cut ends with fewer. | "This cut would make 4097 clips; a project holds at most 4096. Lock a track that needs no cut, such as a music bed, or cut less." |
2059	
2060	Closing the gap can also fail for a reason of its own, such as a linked clip that would have to start before the start of the timeline. That reason shows in the same place.
2061	
2062	## Good to know
2063	
2064	- The cut goes through everything on every unlocked track, including music, captions and tracks you've muted or hidden. A locked track with no words in the cut stays whole and doesn't move, which is the way to keep a music bed in one piece.
2065	- Markers don't move, as with every [ripple delete](/editing/delete-clips/).
2066	
2067	## With an agent
2068	
2069	`get_timeline_transcript` reads the same words, up to 2,000 at a time, and says which can't be cut and why. Each word carries `cut_start` and `cut_end`, the range the tab would cut it by. One `ripple_delete_ranges` call from the first word's `cut_start` to the last word's `cut_end` cuts a run, and `set_range` can shade it first. `get_transcript` reads one clip's words. Neither reading tool uploads anything. If the voice model hasn't heard a file yet, the answer has a note saying its starts are still early, so ask again once it has. See [`get_timeline_transcript`](/mcp/tools-captions/#get_timeline_transcript), [`get_transcript`](/mcp/tools-captions/#get_transcript) and [`ripple_delete_ranges`](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/#ripple_delete_ranges).

2082	---
2083	title: "Shorten a pause"
2084	description: Spot long pauses in the Transcript tab and tighten them, keeping 0.2 s at each end and closing the gap on every unlocked track.
2085	---
2086	
2087	
2088	The Transcript tab marks each long pause in the speech. Click one and delete it to tighten the pause without taking any words, as one undo step.
2089	
2090	<AtAGlance
2091	  menu={['Edit ▸ Delete', 'Edit ▸ Ripple Delete']}
2092	  keys={['⌫', '⌦', '⌘⌫']}
2093	  where="Inspector ▸ Transcript"
2094	  tools={['get_timeline_transcript', 'ripple_delete_ranges', 'set_range']}
2095	  needs="Words in the Transcript tab, and the voice model, which runs on your Mac with no key and no upload."
2096	/>
2097	
2098	## Pauses in the transcript
2099	
2100	Where the speech stops for more than a second between two words of one clip, the transcript shows the pause's length in grey after the word before it, such as `[2.4 s]`.
2101	
2102	The length is what the voice model hears as silence between that word and the next. The model is the one [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) uses. It runs when the project opens the file, so a file's pauses appear once it has finished. They appear for words from an [AssemblyAI transcript](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/) as well as words read on this Mac.
2103	
2104	That second is measured as the clip plays on the timeline, so a clip's speed changes what counts. A 0.8 s silence in a clip slowed to half speed plays for 1.6 s, and shows as a pause.
2105	
2106	## Select a pause
2107	
2108	Click the pause. It's selected on its own, the part that would go becomes the timeline's [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/), and the playhead moves to the start of that cut. To hear what would go, turn on [Loop](/timeline/loop/).
2109	
2110	<kbd>⎋</kbd> clears the selection and the range. Dragging, <kbd>⇧</kbd> and <kbd>⌘A</kbd> select words only, so a pause is always selected by clicking it.
2111	
2112	## Delete the pause
2113	
2114	<Steps>
2115	
2116	1. Choose **View ▸ Transcript** (<kbd>⌃⌘T</kbd>) to open the Transcript tab.
2117	
2118	2. Click the pause, the grey length in the text.
2119	
2120	3. Press <kbd>⌫</kbd>.
2121	
2122	</Steps>
2123	
2124	The pause is shortened, keeping 0.2 s at each end, and the gap closes on every unlocked track, as one undo step named **Delete Pause**. A `[2.4 s]` pause loses about 2 s and leaves about 0.4 s. The range clears and the playhead lands where the cut was.
2125	
2126	<kbd>⌦</kbd>, <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd>, **Edit ▸ Delete** and **Edit ▸ Ripple Delete** do the same, as long as the transcript text has the keyboard.
2127	
2128	The cut lands on whole frames and never takes the start of a word.
2129	
2130	The tab won't cut a pause when a locked track has words inside the cut, or when the cut would pass the limit of 4,096 clips. It beeps and shows the same [reason](/captions/delete-words/#when-the-tab-wont-cut) it gives for words, at the foot of the inspector.
2131	
2132	## When a pause isn't shown
2133	
2134	The tab shows a pause only when it can cut it cleanly. There's no pause marked:
2135	
2136	- between two clips, including the two halves of a clip you've split
2137	- when either word next to it is [faint](/captions/delete-words/#words-that-cant-be-cut): inside a nest, under a transition or on a locked track
2138	- when a word on another track, one the tab shows, reaches into the part that would go, because the cut would take that word
2139	- when a clip whose words haven't been read yet starts inside the cut
2140	- when keeping 0.2 s at each end would leave nothing to cut
2141	
2142	## With an agent
2143	
2144	`get_timeline_transcript` reads the same pauses, each with the range the tab would cut it by, and one [`ripple_delete_ranges`](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/#ripple_delete_ranges) call shortens one. `set_range` can shade that range first. An agent can pass several in that call, which makes them one undo step. See [Cut words and pauses](/mcp/tools-captions/#cut-words-and-pauses).

2158	description: Every key the Transcript tab's text takes, for moving by word or line, selecting, clearing and deleting, and what the rest of the keyboard does there.
2159	---
2160	
2161	
2162	While the transcript text has the keyboard, the arrows move through the words instead of the frames, and the delete keys cut words. Every other key works as it does on the timeline.
2163	
2164	<AtAGlance menu="View ▸ Transcript" keys="⌃⌘T" where="Inspector ▸ Transcript, with the text active" />
2165	
2166	To give the text the keyboard, choose **View ▸ Transcript** (<kbd>⌃⌘T</kbd>) or click in the text. Clicking **Transcript** in the inspector's tab strip shows the tab but doesn't give the text the keyboard.
2167	
2168	| Key | What it does |
2169	| --- | --- |
2170	| <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> | Select the previous or next word and move the playhead to it |
2171	| <kbd>↑</kbd> <kbd>↓</kbd> | Select the nearest word on the line above or below and move the playhead to it |
2172	| <kbd>⇧</kbd> with an arrow | Extend the selection without moving the playhead |
2173	| <kbd>⌘A</kbd> | Select every word |
2174	| <kbd>⎋</kbd> | Clear the selected words or pause |
2175	| <kbd>⌫</kbd> <kbd>⌦</kbd> | Delete the selected words and close the gap, or shorten the selected pause |
2176	
2177	## Move word by word
2178	
2179	<kbd>←</kbd> and <kbd>→</kbd> select the previous or next word and move the playhead to it. If the video is playing, it keeps playing from there.
2180	
2181	They move from the end of the selection you last moved. With a [pause](/captions/shorten-pauses/) selected, they move from the word before it. With nothing selected, they move from the highlighted word, the last one to start at or before the playhead, and if there isn't one, <kbd>→</kbd> selects the first word and <kbd>←</kbd> the last. At the first and last word they stay put.
2182	
2183	## Move line by line
2184	
2185	<kbd>↑</kbd> and <kbd>↓</kbd> select the nearest word on the line above or below, as the text is laid out, and move the playhead to it. They skip the timecode lines, and beep at the first and last line.
2186	
2187	## Extend the selection
2188	
2189	<kbd>⇧</kbd> with any arrow moves one end of the selection and leaves the playhead where it is. The other end stays where you started, so going back the other way shrinks the selection. <kbd>⇧</kbd>-click does the same with the mouse.
2190	
2191	The tab may [widen the selection](/captions/delete-words/#the-selection-becomes-the-range) further, over any word the cut would cut into.
2192	
2193	## Select every word
2194	
2195	<kbd>⌘A</kbd> selects every word, and **Edit ▸ Select All** does the same while the text has the keyboard. It selects words only, so a selected pause is dropped.
2196	
2197	## Clear the selection
2198	
2199	<kbd>⎋</kbd> clears the selected words or pause, along with the range they set. With nothing selected, <kbd>⎋</kbd> does what it does in the rest of the window, which is deselect a selected [action](/motion/actions/).
2200	
2201	## Delete
2202	
2203	With words selected, <kbd>⌫</kbd> or <kbd>⌦</kbd> [deletes them and closes the gap](/captions/delete-words/). With a pause selected, either one [shortens it](/captions/shorten-pauses/). <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> does the same.
2204	
2205	With nothing selected in the text, <kbd>⌫</kbd> and <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> do what they do on the timeline, so they act on the [selected clips or the range](/editing/delete-clips/).
2206
